title: Intraday Patterns in the Cross-section of Stock Returns
one_line: A stock's return in a given half hour predicts its return in the SAME half hour on later days (≈3 bps next day, significant for ~40 days), strongest at the open and close, but the effect is smaller than trading costs in stocks.

findings.statement: Same-half-hour returns persist at daily lags (13, 26, 39 half-hours...), significant for ~40 trading days.
Winners-minus-losers spread ≈ 3.01 bps at the same time next day.
findings.evidence: Smallest t at daily lags in week 1: 9.62.

findings.statement: Strongest in the first and last half hours; relatively stronger at the close for S&P 500 stocks.
After paying spreads the strategies lose money (e.g. −14 to −24 bps).

why.pattern: Predictable demand for immediacy at particular times of day (fund flows, algorithms).

reported_results.headline: ≈3 bps same-slot persistence; unprofitable after spreads.

tradable_edge: Basis for same_slot_seasonality_es; for ES the cost per trade is much lower than for single stocks, but ~3 bps is still below ES round-trip costs — expect it to fail unless the index-level effect is bigger.
angles: Gross vs cost check for same_slot_seasonality_es
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 2), not by the weekly pipeline.
